Subject: Packaging options + questions for ClearPath (usage attached)

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency / cost controls you showed. We're starting an internal review of packaging and want to understand practical fallout for two scenarios:

1) If we start on a compact "feature-first" tier (lower throughput, full feature set) and later need to raise throughput, what does the upgrade path look like?
2) If we start on a throughput-first plan and later need to remove certain premium features, how are credits/prorations handled?

I attached our June usage report so you can see typical peak QPS and token distribution. A few asks we have up front:
- Can you send a one-page matrix that maps feature bundles to SKU consequences (can we keep feature flags when moving tiers?)
- What is the rollback / stepdown policy if we overshoot and need to step down to a lower tier mid-term?
- Do you offer an introductory discount for pilots that converts to a standard list pricing after 90 days?

Procurement is looped on cc; we may need a draft amendment to the MSA depending on the path we pick.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Packaging options + questions for ClearPath (usage attached)

Hi Maya — thanks for the usage file, that helps. High level answers here and I attached a short pack matrix + pilot proposal for clarity. Quick summary:

- Upgrade path (compact -> throughput):
  * We can perform an in-place upgrade that preserves feature flags and entitlements. The typical flow is a 2-week canary (10% traffic) followed by a staged ramp. No rework required on your app unless you pin to model variants with different tokenization profiles.
  * Pricing: you convert from a feature-bundled seat to a throughput reservation; we credit leftover pre-paid feature seat dollars toward the new commitment on a pro-rata basis.

- Downgrade / stepdown (throughput -> compact):
  * Downgrades are allowed at the next billing period with a 30-day notice window. For annual commitments we support a one-time stepdown with a small administrative fee (we document in the draft amendment).
  * Feature-level removal: if you remove premium modules mid-term we issue credit only for fully unused prepaid modules; partial-month credits are pro-rated.

- Pilot discounts: we commonly offer a 30% pilot discount for a single 90-day pilot that converts to list pricing (or a pre-agreed renewal discount). We can propose a conversion uplift clause (e.g., 10% discount for year-one commitment if converted within 45 days of pilot end).

Next steps (suggested):
1) Internal workshop: 45-minute technical + commercial sync (I can run) — proposed slots: Thu 7/26 10:00am PT or Fri 7/27 2:00pm PT.
2) We send a single-page pack matrix and pilot proposal (attached).
3) If procurement wants a draft amendment, we can push a stub and track redlines in DocuSign.

Attaching: redwood_pack_matrix_v2.xlsx; pilot_proposal_clearpath.pdf

Best,

Maya — adding a few technical guardrails for the workshop so the commercial flow maps to operational reality.

Operational notes:
- KV cache and prefix caching: if you move to a throughput model we recommend enabling prefix caching for the top-5 user flows. That preserves latency while lowering token costs during peak. This does not change feature entitlements.
- Quantization/latency packages: Some model variants are cheaper but require a short warmup period after autoscaling events. We surface that in the SLA assumptions and in the pilot scope.
- Rollback mechanics: The canary is reversible at any stage; the staged ramp is automated and will fall back to the previous pool if error rates exceed thresholds. We track this as an ops playbook item.

Commercially relevant operational limits:
- Canary length: default 2 weeks (can shorten to 4 business days for pilots).
- Stepdown effective date: first day of next billing cycle unless otherwise agreed (we can include an exception in the amendment).

Connor — happy to take ~10 minutes in the workshop to walk them through the ops playbook and show the canary rollback trace sample.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Ops | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
